newsitem.title: FRANCE: French hotels say business picked up in August.
newsitem.headline: French hotels say business picked up in August.

text.p: After a slow start to the summer, business at French hotels picked up in August, thanks partly to the strength of the Italian lira and pound sterling against the French franc, the National Federation of Hoteliers (FNIH) said on Tuesday.
"The 1997 season looks, halfway through, to be a good year," FNIH said in a statement.

The FNIH said poor weather adversely affected business in June and the first half of July, leaving activity in July slightly down compared with 1997, but business picked up at the end of July and so far August has been a "clear success."
FNIH said foreign tourists were behind the increase in occupancy rates.
The French restaurant industry, however, was suffering a further decline in business, continuing the trend seen during the past four years.
